en.text:
Today’s M&A briefing — 8 deals, the strategies behind them · 22 November 2026

🔹 FedEx (consortium avec Advent International, A&R Capital and PPF) (express transport and international logistics) finalizes the acquisition of InPost (automated parcel locker network and parcel delivery, dominant in Poland, also present in France and the UK) — €7.8bn.
InPost operates a physical point infrastructure integrated into e-commerce merchant sales funnels, with tens of millions of European consumers already accustomed to the network. The acquisition concludes a process initiated in February.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: FedEx is not acquiring additional logistics capabilities but rather a direct relationship with tens of millions of European consumers who have already changed their behavior — a radically different model from its long-distance B2B logistics.

🔹 Cegid (management, accounting, payroll) acquires Shine (professional neobank and financial management tool for freelancers, micro-entrepreneurs, and VSEs, France).
Shine (formerly Ageras in France) has 420,000 clients, employs 400 people, and generates €100M in revenue.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: By acquiring Shine, Cegid gains access to the behavioral database of 420,000 rapidly growing independent workers — a population its ecosystem did not directly reach until now.

🔹 Deutz (manufacturing of industrial engines) finalizes the acquisition of FFG (Familienbetrieb Fahrzeugwerke Falkenried) (construction and reconditioning of industrial vehicles).
The stated rationale focuses on new incoming contracts; the share of profits will be decisive in judging the success of the operation.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: Under pressure from the energy transition, Deutz seeks to diversify its outlets towards fleet maintenance and conversion, recurring revenues less volatile than the sale of new engines.

🔹 Green Mobility Holding acquires Deutsche Dienstrad (company bike leasing for employees via employers).
The company bike market has grown significantly in Germany due to tax advantages.

🔹 Serco Group (government services provider, defense, healthcare) acquires QinetiQ's US division (defense and technology services established and accredited in the United States, originating from the British QinetiQ group).

🔹 Webuild (civil construction and engineering on large infrastructure projects, tunnels, dams, subways, water, Italy) takes control of Trevi (special foundations and geotechnical works).

🔹 Kemkens acquires Hajnadi.
Kemkens is a Dutch technical installer (HVAC, electricity, plumbing). It is acquiring Hajnadi and Knibbeler, two companies in the same sector in the Netherlands.

🔹 Hollandia Infra (metal construction and infrastructure, Netherlands) takes over Solidd (steel construction, Sumar, Friesland, Netherlands).

🔗 These deals and those of your markets, every morning: https://proplace.co/actualites/?lang=en&secteurs=fintech,industrial-tech-and-manufacturing,mobility-and-transportation,construction-and-proptech&type=ma

fr.text:
M&A : les 8 annonces récentes de l'édito du 22 novembre 2026.

🔹 FedEx (consortium avec Advent International, A&R Capital et PPF) (𝑡𝑟𝑎𝑛𝑠𝑝𝑜𝑟𝑡 𝑒𝑥𝑝𝑟𝑒𝑠𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑙𝑜𝑔𝑖𝑠𝑡𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒 𝑖𝑛𝑡𝑒𝑟𝑛𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑎𝑙𝑒) finalise le rachat de InPost (𝑟𝑒́𝑠𝑒𝑎𝑢 𝑑𝑒 𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑠𝑖𝑔𝑛𝑒𝑠 𝑎𝑢𝑡𝑜𝑚𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑙𝑖𝑣𝑟𝑎𝑖𝑠𝑜𝑛 𝑑𝑒 𝑐𝑜𝑙𝑖𝑠, 𝑑𝑜𝑚𝑖𝑛𝑎𝑛𝑡 𝑒𝑛 𝑃𝑜𝑙𝑜𝑔𝑛𝑒, 𝑝𝑟𝑒́𝑠𝑒𝑛𝑡 𝑒𝑛 𝐹𝑟𝑎𝑛𝑐𝑒 𝑒𝑡 𝑎𝑢 𝑅𝑜𝑦𝑎𝑢𝑚𝑒-𝑈𝑛𝑖) — 7,8 Md€.
InPost opère une infrastructure de points physiques intégrée dans les tunnels de vente des marchands e-commerce, avec des dizaines de millions de consommateurs européens déjà habitués au réseau. L'acquisition conclut un processus engagé en février.

🔹 Cegid (𝑙𝑜𝑔𝑖𝑐𝑖𝑒𝑙𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑔𝑒𝑠𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛, 𝑐𝑜𝑚𝑝𝑡𝑎𝑏𝑖𝑙𝑖𝑡𝑒́, 𝑝𝑎𝑖𝑒) rachète Shine (𝑛𝑒́𝑜𝑏𝑎𝑛𝑞𝑢𝑒 𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑓𝑒𝑠𝑠𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑛𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑒 𝑒𝑡 𝑜𝑢𝑡𝑖𝑙 𝑑𝑒 𝑔𝑒𝑠𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑓𝑖𝑛𝑎𝑛𝑐𝑖𝑒̀𝑟𝑒 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑖𝑛𝑑𝑒́𝑝𝑒𝑛𝑑𝑎𝑛𝑡𝑠, 𝑚𝑖𝑐𝑟𝑜-𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑟𝑒𝑝𝑟𝑒𝑛𝑒𝑢𝑟𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑇𝑃𝐸, 𝐹𝑟𝑎𝑛𝑐𝑒).
Shine (anciennement Ageras en France) compte 420 000 clients, emploie 400 personnes et génère 100 M€ de chiffre d'affaires.

🔹 Deutz (𝑓𝑎𝑏𝑟𝑖𝑐𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑𝑒 𝑚𝑜𝑡𝑒𝑢𝑟𝑠 𝑖𝑛𝑑𝑢𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑒𝑙𝑠) finalise le rachat de FFG (Familienbetrieb Fahrzeugwerke Falkenried) (𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑢𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑒𝑡 𝑟𝑒𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑑𝑖𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑛𝑒𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡 𝑑𝑒 𝑣𝑒́ℎ𝑖𝑐𝑢𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝑖𝑛𝑑𝑢𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑖𝑒𝑙𝑠).
Le rationnel affiché porte sur de nouveaux contrats entrants ; la part des bénéfices sera déterminante pour juger du succès de l'opération.

🔹 Green Mobility Holding rachète Deutsche Dienstrad (𝑙𝑒𝑎𝑠𝑖𝑛𝑔 𝑑𝑒 𝑣𝑒́𝑙𝑜𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑓𝑜𝑛𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑠𝑎𝑙𝑎𝑟𝑖𝑒́𝑠).
Le marché du vélo de fonction a fortement progressé en Allemagne sous l'effet d'avantages fiscaux.

🔹 Serco Group (𝑝𝑟𝑒𝑠𝑡𝑎𝑡𝑎𝑖𝑟𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑠𝑒𝑟𝑣𝑖𝑐𝑒𝑠 𝑎𝑢𝑥 𝑔𝑜𝑢𝑣𝑒𝑟𝑛𝑒𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡𝑠, 𝑑𝑒́𝑓𝑒𝑛𝑠𝑒) rachète la division américaine de QinetiQ (𝑠𝑒𝑟𝑣𝑖𝑐𝑒𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑑𝑒́𝑓𝑒𝑛𝑠𝑒 𝑒𝑡 𝑑𝑒 𝑡𝑒𝑐ℎ𝑛𝑜𝑙𝑜𝑔𝑖𝑒 𝑖𝑚𝑝𝑙𝑎𝑛𝑡𝑒́𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑎𝑐𝑐𝑟𝑒́𝑑𝑖𝑡𝑒́𝑠 𝑎𝑢𝑥 𝐸́𝑡𝑎𝑡𝑠-𝑈𝑛𝑖𝑠, 𝑖𝑠𝑠𝑢𝑠 𝑑𝑢 𝑔𝑟𝑜𝑢𝑝𝑒 𝑏𝑟𝑖𝑡𝑎𝑛𝑛𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒 𝑄𝑖𝑛𝑒𝑡𝑖𝑄).

🔹 Webuild (𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑢𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑒𝑡 𝑖𝑛𝑔𝑒́𝑛𝑖𝑒𝑟𝑖𝑒 𝑐𝑖𝑣𝑖𝑙𝑒 𝑠𝑢𝑟 𝑔𝑟𝑎𝑛𝑑𝑠 𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑗𝑒𝑡𝑠 𝑑'𝑖𝑛𝑓𝑟𝑎𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑢𝑐𝑡𝑢𝑟𝑒, 𝑡𝑢𝑛𝑛𝑒𝑙𝑠, 𝑏𝑎𝑟𝑟𝑎𝑔𝑒𝑠, 𝑚𝑒́𝑡𝑟𝑜𝑠, 𝑒𝑎𝑢, 𝐼𝑡𝑎𝑙𝑖𝑒) prend le contrôle de Trevi (𝑓𝑜𝑛𝑑𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑠 𝑠𝑝𝑒́𝑐𝑖𝑎𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑡𝑟𝑎𝑣𝑎𝑢𝑥 𝑔𝑒́𝑜𝑡𝑒𝑐ℎ𝑛𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒𝑠).

🔹 Kemkens acquiert Hajnadi.

🔹 Hollandia Infra (𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑢𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑚𝑒́𝑡𝑎𝑙𝑙𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒 𝑒𝑡 𝑖𝑛𝑓𝑟𝑎𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑢𝑐𝑡𝑢𝑟𝑒𝑠) reprend Solidd (𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑢𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑒𝑛 𝑎𝑐𝑖𝑒𝑟, 𝑆𝑢𝑚𝑎𝑟, 𝐹𝑟𝑖𝑠𝑒, 𝑃𝑎𝑦𝑠-𝐵𝑎𝑠).

en.text:
Today’s fundraising briefing — one deal, the strategy behind it · 22 November 2026

🔹 Mistral AI (development of open-weight and API-based large language models, a European alternative to American models, France) — €100m.
Mistral distributes its models open-weight and via API, positioning itself as a European alternative to OpenAI and Anthropic. Deutsche Telekom becomes a direct distribution channel to thousands of German industrial companies.
𝗨𝘀𝗲 𝗼𝗳 𝗳𝘂𝗻𝗱𝘀: Deployment of Mistral models to German SMEs and industrial Mittelstand via Deutsche Telekom.
𝗜𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿𝘀: Deutsche Telekom, German telecoms operator aiming to deploy Mistral models in German industry.
𝗢𝘂𝗿 𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄: By taking a stake in Mistral rather than licensing an American model, Deutsche Telekom gains a governance position in the player for which it becomes the main industrial distribution channel in Europe.

fr.text:
Levées de fonds : 1 opération chiffrée de l'édito du 22 novembre 2026.

🔹 Mistral AI (𝑑𝑒́𝑣𝑒𝑙𝑜𝑝𝑝𝑒𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡 𝑑𝑒 𝑔𝑟𝑎𝑛𝑑𝑠 𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑒̀𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑙𝑎𝑛𝑔𝑎𝑔𝑒 𝑜𝑝𝑒𝑛-𝑤𝑒𝑖𝑔ℎ𝑡 𝑒𝑡 𝑣𝑖𝑎 𝐴𝑃𝐼, 𝑎𝑙𝑡𝑒𝑟𝑛𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑣𝑒 𝑒𝑢𝑟𝑜𝑝𝑒́𝑒𝑛𝑛𝑒 𝑎𝑢𝑥 𝑚𝑜𝑑𝑒̀𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝑎𝑚𝑒́𝑟𝑖𝑐𝑎𝑖𝑛𝑠, 𝐹𝑟𝑎𝑛𝑐𝑒) — 100 M€.
Mistral distribue ses modèles en open-weight et via API et se positionne comme alternative européenne à OpenAI et Anthropic. Deutsche Telekom devient un canal de distribution direct vers des milliers d'entreprises industrielles allemandes.
𝗢𝗯𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗳 : Déploiement des modèles Mistral auprès des PME et du Mittelstand industriel allemand via Deutsche Telekom.
𝗔𝘃𝗲𝗰 : Deutsche Telekom, opérateur télécoms allemand visant le déploiement des modèles Mistral dans l'industrie allemande.
𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁 𝗱𝗲 𝘃𝘂𝗲 : En prenant une participation dans Mistral plutôt que de s'adosser à un modèle américain sous licence, Deutsche Telekom se donne une position dans la gouvernance de l'acteur dont elle devient le principal canal de distribution industrielle en Europe.
